title: Signature TEE Measurement Registry
description: Signature edition: every enclave build's measurements are registered with its source version and audit status — the allowlist is a queryable registry, not a text file. Deployments verify against the registry; unregistered measurements never get secrets. This is a Signature original method.
method: Register (measurement, source version, audit) per build; deployments query the registry; unregistered = no secrets.
usage: Register every release build; audit before registering; query at every provisioning.

demo.code:
print('MRENCLAVE a1b2 -> build v2.3, audited 2026-10-21')
print('provision: registry HIT -> secrets released')

title: Signature ARM TrustZone
description: Signature edition: TrustZone splits the processor into secure and normal worlds, with the secure world running trusted apps (keystore, DRM, biometric matching) isolated by hardware. It's the TEE in billions of phones — smaller and more embedded-focused than SGX, with the secure monitor mediating world switches.
method: Trusted apps run in the secure world; normal world calls via SMC; the secure monitor enforces isolation.
usage: Keep trusted apps minimal; the secure world is high-value attack surface.

demo.code:
print('secure world: keystore TA; normal world: android app')
print('SMC call: sign(data) -> signature (keys never leave secure world)')

title: Signature Confidential containers
description: Signature edition: Confidential containers (CoCo, Azure ACI) run standard container images inside TEEs — no enclave rewrite needed. The container runtime is measured and attested; the image's layers are verified. It's TEE adoption without the porting tax.
method: Run images under the confidential runtime; attest the runtime + image measurements; standard orchestration outside.
usage: Verify image signatures; attest before scheduling sensitive workloads.

demo.code:
print('pod scheduled on CoCo runtime; image signature + measurement verified')
print('container runs with memory encrypted')

title: Signature Sealing data to enclaves
description: Signature edition: Sealing encrypts data so only the same enclave (same MRENCLAVE, or same signer) can unseal it later — persistent secrets bound to the code identity. Sealed keys survive reboots but not code changes (unless sealed to the signer), tying data to the exact trusted code.
method: Seal with the enclave's seal key; store ciphertext outside; unseal only in the matching enclave; choose MRENCLAVE vs MRSIGNER policy deliberately.
usage: Choose the seal policy for your upgrade story; back up sealed data knowing it binds to code identity.

demo.code:
print('sealed: master_key (policy: MRSIGNER)')
print('upgraded enclave (same signer): unseal OK; different signer: DENIED')

title: Signature TEE key management services
description: Signature edition: The canonical TEE workload: keys live and are used inside the enclave — generated there, never exported, operations performed inside. Cloud HSMs and private CAs run this way: the key's entire lifecycle happens behind the hardware boundary.
method: Generate keys in-enclave; expose only operations (sign, decrypt); attest before trusting; log operations outside.
usage: Never export private keys; audit the operation logs; rotate on schedule.

demo.code:
print('CA key generated in-enclave (never exported)')
print('sign(csr) -> certificate; key never left the boundary')

title: Signature Multi-TEE portability
description: Signature edition: SGX, TrustZone, SEV, TDX all differ; portable TEE frameworks (Open Enclave, Veracruz) abstract the differences so one codebase runs across TEEs. Portability avoids hardware lock-in and lets deployments choose the TEE per environment — write once, attest everywhere.
method: Build on a portable framework; abstract attestation verification; test on each target TEE.
usage: Abstract early; verify attestation semantics per TEE (they differ in details).

demo.code:
print('same codebase: SGX in cloud, TrustZone on edge')
print('attestation abstracted; per-TEE verifiers plugged in')

title: Signature Enclave attestation flows
description: Signature edition: Attestation is the TEE's trust handshake: the enclave produces a signed quote of its measurements; the verifier checks the signature chain to the hardware root and compares measurements to known-good values; only then are secrets provisioned. Every TEE integration lives or dies on getting this flow right.
method: Generate quote in-enclave; verify signature chain; compare MRENCLAVE/MRSIGNER to allowlist; provision secrets on success.
usage: Pin the verification logic; allowlist measurements per release; never provision before verification.

demo.code:
print('quote: MRENCLAVE=a1b2, signed by Intel')
print('verify: chain OK, measurement allowlisted -> provision API keys')

title: Signature AMD SEV-SNP
description: Signature edition: SEV-SNP encrypts entire VM memory so the hypervisor can't read guest data, with integrity protection against replay and remapping. It's the cloud TEE: lift-and-shift confidential VMs without rewriting apps into enclaves — attestation covers the whole VM launch measurement.
method: Launch VMs with SEV-SNP; verify the attestation report (launch measurement); run unmodified workloads inside.
usage: Verify attestation before migrating sensitive workloads; understand the TCB (firmware + hypervisor still partly trusted).

demo.code:
print('VM launched under SEV-SNP: memory encrypted, integrity protected')
print('attestation report: measurement matches golden -> workload migrated')

title: Signature Intel TDX
description: Signature edition: TDX extends the VM-level confidential computing model to Intel: trust domains are hardware-isolated VMs the hypervisor can't inspect, with attestation via SGX-based quoting. The cloud-native answer for Intel shops — confidential VMs without enclave rewrites.
method: Deploy trust domains; attest via TD quotes; manage like VMs with confidential guarantees.
usage: Use for confidential cloud VMs on Intel; verify quotes in your deployment pipeline.

demo.code:
print('trust domain deployed; TD quote verified')
print('hypervisor sees ciphertext only')
